subject: science
passage: In a bullfight, the matador waves a red cape, and the bull charges at it. Because of this, many people believe that the color red makes bulls angry. The idea is so widely accepted that a person who provokes someone is sometimes said to be waving a red flag at a bull.
passage_b: Cattle have only two kinds of color-sensing cells in their eyes, and they cannot tell red from green. What a bull reacts to is the movement of the cloth. Matadors also use a much larger cape that is pink on one side and yellow on the other, and bulls charge at it just as readily. The cape is red for the audience, not for the bull.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the belief in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that the color red makes bulls especially angry
choices.B: By noting that bulls can see more colors than people can
choices.C: By suggesting that bulls charge only when they feel threatened
choices.D: By explaining that the bull reacts to the cape's movement rather than its color

explanation.why: Text 1 says people believe "the color red makes bulls angry." Text 2 answers that bulls "cannot tell red from green" and that "what a bull reacts to is the movement of the cloth," adding that bulls charge a pink-and-yellow cape just as readily. So the author of Text 2 would reply that movement, not color, draws the charge.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says bulls cannot even tell red from green, so its author would not agree.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says cattle have only two kinds of color-sensing cells, which means they see fewer colors, not more.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 never discusses whether bulls feel threatened.
explanation.D: Correct. Text 2 says bulls cannot see red and react to the cloth's movement.
